teaser.text: ResMed sells the equipment, supplies, software, and services that help people breathe and sleep at home. To understand its business, follow one dollar from a prescribed machine to the provider who buys it, the patient who uses it, and the costs ResMed pays to make the system work.

stock.title: ResMed stock forecast
stock.meta_description: ResMed stock forecast: $249.58 in October 2027 and $286.46 in October 2029, across bear, base and bull cases.
stock.opening: The weighted ResMed scenario is $249.58 in October 2027. It hinges on durable patient continuation and cash generation while ResMed defends share and resolves Astral.
stock.closing: The full ResMed memo also answers how ResMed’s business works, who its rivals are, how management operates, and what risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: Where could ResMed’s shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is $249.58 in October 2027, a 5% total return including dividends. It reaches $272.52 in October 2028, a 16% return. By October 2029, the weighted price is $286.46, a 23% return. The three-year range runs from $186.18 in the bear case to $454.58 in the bull case, against today’s $239.77.
The final scenario probabilities are 25% bear, 60% base and 15% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for ResMed?

paragraphs.text: The bear case lowers earnings to $1,619 million in the first window and $1,636 million in the second. It reaches $1,657 million in the third. Philips may regain share, Astral remains suspended, MatrixCare leaves the portfolio and GLP-1 treatment or provider capacity may slow starts and resupply. The bull case reaches $1,829 million, then $1,999 million and $2,178 million as home testing, virtual care, adherence and manufacturing efficiency exceed the base path.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for ResMed today?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow tests whether accounting profit becomes spendable cash. ResMed generated about US$1.6 billion of free cash flow in FY2026 after capital spending, and management can use it for research, acquisitions, debt repayment, dividends or buybacks. Enterprise value compares the operating business with EBITDA, or earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, but depreciation still reflects equipment that must be replaced. Book value has the same limitation because goodwill from acquisitions may not equal the value of patient relationships or software.

dividend.opening: The forecast starts from a $0.66 quarterly rate; its annual dividend is $2.64 in the bear case, $2.706, $2.9844 and $3.28284 in the base case, and $2.7192, $3.045504 and $3.41096448 in the bull case. Its free cash flow exceeded net income in FY2026, although it fell slightly from FY2025 as capital spending increased and more cash moved into operating needs.
dividend.closing: The full ResMed memo also covers its business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does ResMed pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start from the $0.66 quarterly rate. The bear case holds the annual dividend at $2.64 because the board may pause increases. The base case assumes another 10% annual increase, producing $2.706, $2.9844 and $3.28284 across the three windows. The bull case assumes 12% increases, producing $2.7192, $3.045504 and $3.41096448. The base path follows five years of increases and the latest 10% raise, while the bear path allows for Astral, portfolio and cash demands.

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow starts with cash from operations and subtracts purchases of property, plant and equipment. In FY2026, free cash flow exceeded net income, which supports the quality of reported earnings. It nevertheless fell slightly from FY2025 because capital spending increased and more cash moved into operating needs.

After the repair, buybacks accelerated and distributions claimed a larger share of free cash flow. ResMed still retained cash for acquisitions and other investment, while new-share proceeds mean gross repurchases should not be confused with the net reduction in shares outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The first base-case test is fiscal 2027 guidance: core constant-currency revenue growth of 5%–7% and EPS of $12.00–$12.25. Continued device and mask demand, manufacturing efficiency and cash generation would support the base case through 2028 and 2029.

The view moves toward the bear case if Philips wins back provider orders during 2027–2029, Astral’s suspension and remediation persist, or GLP-1 treatment and provider capacity slow starts and mask resupply.

earnings.title: ResMed earnings: October 29, 2026 results
earnings.meta_description: ResMed reports on October 29, 2026; see its guidance, past delivery, eight-quarter results and what to watch next.
earnings.opening: ResMed's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. Watch whether ResMed turns adjusted growth into cash while comparing headline sales with core sales.
earnings.closing: The full ResMed memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has ResMed guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: For the year ending June 2027, ResMed forecasts revenue of $5.75 billion–$5.85 billion. It forecasts non-GAAP earnings per share of $12.00–$12.25, representing growth of 7%–10%. Non-GAAP means management excludes selected accounting charges from its preferred performance measure.

The core comparison is designed to show how the continuing business is performing. Core constant-currency growth of 5%–7% holds exchange rates steady and compares similar businesses. ResMed includes only two months of MatrixCare revenue in each comparison year and excludes Noctrix revenue. Reported revenue still includes Noctrix and a 50-basis-point currency headwind. Transition-service agreements should largely offset costs left behind by the MatrixCare sale during the first year.

blocks.heading: What did ResMed say about past promises?

paragraphs.text: ResMed also kept one measurable promise. In April 2026, management reiterated a gross-margin outlook of 62–63%. FY26 non-GAAP gross margin was 62.4%, inside that range. On balance, equity pay creates genuine downside for executives, but the board should judge adjusted bonuses alongside reported profit, dilution and cash generation. That is the standard by which owners can decide whether ResMed’s leadership is truly on their side.

blocks.heading: What happened to ResMed revenue and profit over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew 8.6% from the June 2025 quarter, or approximately 8% at constant currency. The quarterly sequence shows continuing expansion rather than a sudden demand collapse, although the latest growth rate was slower than the preceding quarters.

blocks.heading: What should people watch in ResMed's next results?

paragraphs.text: The October 29, 2026 results call should show the first quarter of fiscal 2027 after the MatrixCare disposal, the enlarged repurchase program and the Noctrix acquisition. Compare headline sales with core sales, then compare cash generation with spending. Normal seasonal revenue movement and slightly lower year-over-year first-quarter gross margin would not, by themselves, disprove the annual plan.
